scope: Provenance and fitting exposure for the completed task-reference families of Table 3. No optional old baseline is relabelled required or newly run.

baselines.label: RW3 (local formula fit)

fitting_exposure.parameter_fit: 25 original training participants; 28,000 free choices; forced choices retained for updates
fitting_exposure.autonomous_evaluation: 31 original timelines including the 25 training-participant timelines; 34,720 free choices
fitting_exposure.autonomous_action_rule: Softmax sampling at temperature 1 with original participant seeds

baselines.comparison_note: Same Horizon target modes and published split; task fitting and softmax readout differ from frozen neural native-action protocols. Autonomous reward is not held-out reward evidence. The unavailable author executable and its archived NLL are distinct references.

baselines.label: Independent end-to-end ANN (reimplementation)

fitting_exposure.split_unit: Original response/trial fold within each participant; not held-out participants
fitting_exposure.checkpoint_selection: Lowest loss on that same validation fold across all 3,000 iterations; not nested model selection
fitting_exposure.neural_models: Frozen checkpoints without this task-specific fitting

baselines.comparison_note: Same 163,135 human action targets and original folds. ANN uses disclosed structured inputs and within-participant fitting; neural models use their frozen text/choice interfaces. Validation-fold checkpoint selection and training exposure differ, so this is not a matched-training superiority comparison.

baselines.label: Multiple-cue formula reimplementation

fitting_exposure.parameter_fits: Each of three original experiments fitted separately on its training rows
fitting_exposure.parameter_selection: Held-out data not used for parameter selection
fitting_exposure.feedback: Update only after feedback actually visible to the human; retain no-feedback rows

baselines.comparison_note: Same original held-out human-response mode, split and all responses. Disclosed formula fit is distinct from unrecovered author fitting code and archived unpaired scores. Retain each output interface and NLL definition; shared task membership does not make integer, typed or binned likelihoods interchangeable.

baselines.label: RLWM archived fitted cognitive models

fitting_exposure.fitting: Archived individual parameters fitted on these same 79 participants
fitting_exposure.history: Archive uses RT-filtered histories; neural inputs retain earlier fast responses and omissions

baselines.comparison_note: Same broad offline human-response prediction family, but same-participant fitting and different history exposure. These are neither held-out predictions nor matched-training/identical-history superiority comparisons. Correct-action probability is distinct from an argmax action.

baselines.label: SL (local refit)

fitting_exposure.split: First 75 original source participants are test; remaining 300 are training

baselines.comparison_note: Same test participants and task-mode targets; training exposure and recorded inference rules differ from frozen neural checkpoints. Autonomous modes replay human-source rule-switch times. The four-decimal paper table is the source precision shown here.
baselines.full_precision_source_status: Rounded manuscript table used for this public export; original completed reference is not marked incomplete
baselines.implementation_boundary: Model and objective extracted directly from official SL_model_fitting_and_eval notebook cells; local full refit preserves grid order and tie rule. Generative evaluation samples and updates from its own chosen action.

baselines.label: MetaGreedy (official implementation)

fitting_exposure.fit: Five-fold cross-validation within each participant, with 100 successful Sobol restarts per fit
fitting_exposure.heldout_unit: Trials/action distributions within participants, not unseen participants

baselines.comparison_note: Matches the human-action prediction mode only. Its human-response NLL is not comparable numerically with the 23,750-episode neural autonomous reveals or returns. Project-local Julia 1.4-compatible dependencies differ from the historical author archive environment.
baselines.implementation_boundary: Official source with disclosed local dependency environment; not identical historical environment
baselines.full_precision_source_status: Rounded manuscript description used for this public export; original completed reference is not marked incomplete

baselines.label: Median report of training participants

fitting_exposure.fit: 19,740 reports from the 128 Psych-101 training participants of the same source experiments

baselines.comparison_note: Predicts each test response with the median report of the training participants for the same query in the same experiment.

baselines.label: Rescorla-Wagner with separate learning rates

fitting_exposure.fit: Learning rates 0.08 and 0.06 and inverse temperature 794.328 selected by mean earned reward on 100 independent training environments; no human data
fitting_exposure.evaluation: The ten original test environments, after selection

baselines.comparison_note: CogBench model with separate learning rates for positive and negative prediction errors. Reads only visible information.

baselines.label: Fixed pump threshold per balloon letter

fitting_exposure.fit: Thresholds 61, 63 and 66 selected by mean reward on 100 independent training environments; no human data
fitting_exposure.evaluation: The 20 original test runs, after selection

baselines.comparison_note: The original runner reassigns the three maxima to the letters in every run, so these visible-information thresholds stay below the full-information optimum of 14.00, which requires the hidden maxima.

baselines.label: Later-reward rate of Psych-101 participants

fitting_exposure.fit: None; descriptive summary of human sessions
fitting_exposure.evaluation: All 13,232 participants on the same instrument

baselines.comparison_note: Applies the realized-question rule of the model rows. Human sessions keep four anomaly items that the CogBench path skips after three immediate choices; dropping them gives 39.8%.

baselines.label: Hybrid model fits to CogBench participants (Daw et al. 2011)

fitting_exposure.fit: Seven parameters by maximum likelihood on each of the 40 CogBench human participants
fitting_exposure.evaluation: Identical seeded reward-rate path of the five models

baselines.comparison_note: Twenty-five of the 40 fits have at least one parameter at a bound, so the parameters are a reference policy, not estimates of individual learning.

baselines.label: Other participants, leave one out

fitting_exposure.fit: None; the other participants' responses to the same item, add-one smoothing

baselines.comparison_note: Predicts each human response from the other participants' responses to the same item.

baselines.label: Other participants, leave one out

fitting_exposure.fit: None; the other participants' responses to the same item, add-one smoothing

baselines.comparison_note: Predicts each human response from the other participants' responses to the same item.

baselines.label: Human split-half

fitting_exposure.fit: None; mean reports of two random halves of each item's respondents

baselines.comparison_note: A half-panel mean lies about twice as far from the other half as from the full-panel mean, so this value is a conservative human reference.

baselines.label: Lookup table

fitting_exposure.fit: Response-frequency tables with add-alpha smoothing. Grammar tables on 3,192 training sessions; logic by tenfold cross-fitting across logic participants
fitting_exposure.evaluation: 323 grammar test sessions; held-out logic folds

baselines.comparison_note: Lookup-table family of Binz et al. (2025). The source defines no baseline for the logic set. Transferring the grammar tables to logic instead gives 1.917.

baselines.label: Uniform

fitting_exposure.fit: None; no model and no fitting
fitting_exposure.evaluation: Expectation under the original scoring rule

baselines.comparison_note: Expectation over uniform legal actions or reports with source weights and tie credit. Not a sampled model run. Each row of reference_results.json states its definition.

baselines.label: WADD

fitting_exposure.fit: Four-weight paper-form reimplementation; 7,008 responses from 73 training participants

baselines.comparison_note: Follows the published model family of Binz et al. (2025). An existing fitted output, aligned to the current target with no new model call.

baselines.label: GCM

fitting_exposure.fit: Paper-form reimplementation; 29,776 responses from 85 training participants

baselines.comparison_note: Follows the published model family of Binz et al. (2025). Compares each saved legal argmax to the original objective label under human history; not a human-likelihood or autonomous-reward score.

baselines.label: GCM

fitting_exposure.fit: Train-only refit on 34,200 learning responses across the two source experiments

baselines.comparison_note: Uses the local train-only refit, not the separately archived author-parameter replay. The separate 336 no-feedback classifications and 336 typicality reports are not counted, and the full 6,972-response human-likelihood task is not claimed complete.

baselines.label: GCM

fitting_exposure.fit: Paper-form reimplementation; 4,600 responses from 23 training participants

baselines.comparison_note: Follows the published model family of Binz et al. (2025). Compares each saved legal argmax to the original objective label under human history.

baselines.label: Rational conditional-response model

fitting_exposure.fit: Conditional-response matrix fitted on 34,714 responses from 471 training participants

baselines.comparison_note: The prompt supplies the current letter set, and the fitted model selects the correct visible-set membership category on every item. This does not demonstrate an internal working-memory mechanism.

baselines.label: Thompson family

fitting_exposure.fit: None; the policies observe only their own past selected arms and rewards

baselines.comparison_note: Official Beta(1,1) Thompson on eight Bernoulli conditions and disclosed normal-inverse-gamma Thompson on eight Gaussian conditions. Same original conditions, horizons and environment seeds, with separate logged action RNGs. Step-weighted; no reward units are pooled.

baselines.label: Two-parameter Q-learning

fitting_exposure.fit: Alpha 0.44 and beta 100 selected by mean earned reward on 100 independent 80-trial environments; no human data
fitting_exposure.evaluation: The ten original test environments, after selection

baselines.comparison_note: Original choice equations in the retained CogBench environment. Mean reward 54.6679. No confidence mapping is fitted, and softmax choice probabilities are not read as confidence.

baselines.label: MetaGreedy, archived fitted parameters

fitting_exposure.fit: All 95 archived participant-specific fitted parameter sets; no fitting on the generated evaluation trees
fitting_exposure.evaluation: The same trees as the five open models

baselines.comparison_note: Python port checked against all 20,363 saved Julia probability vectors. The sampler matches the original distribution, not Julia's random stream. Distinct from the archived human-prediction NLL of 1.3670.

baselines.label: Exact Bayes

fitting_exposure.fit: None; the analytic posterior from the visible priors, likelihoods and observations

baselines.comparison_note: Zero by construction. examples/bayes_event_agent.py computes it through the original scorer.

baselines.label: ToMi answer key

fitting_exposure.fit: None; the answer key itself

baselines.comparison_note: ToMi has no human responses, so the reference is the answer key itself; it is 100 by definition, not a measured performance.

comparison_policy: Keep each reference mode, metric, aggregation and training exposure visible.
Same task membership does not imply a matched mode, history, output interface, training exposure or score.
Horizon reward includes training-participant timelines; Hybrid/Mouselab folds are within participants; RLWM archived fits are same-participant references.
Paper-table or paragraph precision is legitimate reported precision and is labelled as such. The inability to locate a full-precision scalar in this bounded export is not an incomplete experiment.
The existing results.json remains unchanged and includes Gaussian Thompson condition results separately.
